label: Divorce legalization year
reliability_criteria: Canonical tier = a curated table of 38 countries, one row each, every row citing the open web page it was read from (read 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-18) and quoting the statement it relies on. Low: the sources are secondary (Wikipedia, encyclopedias, comparative-law reports, journal articles, a few legal collections), not always the statute itself, and rows were assembled by hand from page text; several rows come from pages about something else (a biography, a dictatorship, a thesis). Where divorce was available under religious law before the first STATE law (Hungary, Greece, Latvia, Russia...), the row dates the first state law and says so in its note. Countries whose divorce has no single datable law (the Nordic countries, Germany, the Netherlands, Canada, India with its religious personal laws, most Muslim-majority countries...) are ABSENT; the Philippines and the Vatican, where divorce is not legal, are absent too. The United Kingdom row is the date for England (the sources say England). No witness tier: no machine-readable door carries the series (probed 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-18).
license: Facts with citation (small extracts, clearly attributed) - see docs/licenses.md and catalog/curated/README.md.
notes: Start of the legal availability of divorce in the regime still in force (decision 24; perimeter widened by decision 30 to datable laws of any century and to modern codes). Sources: the list 'countries that have relatively recently legalized divorce' of Wikipedia's Divorce article (Italy 1970, Portugal 1975, Brazil 1977, Spain 1981, Argentina 1987, Paraguay 1991, Colombia 1991, Andorra 1995, Ireland 1996, Chile 2004, Malta 2011), Panama 1911 from the Divorce law by country table, seven rows read from other Wikipedia articles on 2026-10-18 (France 1884, United Kingdom 1857, New Zealand 1867, Uruguay 1907, Venezuela 1904, Mexico 1914, Austria 1938), and nineteen rows read from open pages found by a regional search on 2026-10-18 (Switzerland 1874, Liechtenstein 1974, Poland 1946, Czechia 1919, Hungary 1895, Greece 1920, Latvia 1921, Russia 1917, Cuba 1918, Ecuador 1902, Peru 1930, Bolivia 1932, Dominican Republic 1897, El Salvador 1894, Guatemala 1894, Jamaica 1879, China 1950, Uganda 1904, Yugoslavia 1946). HONEST LIMITS: 38 countries; every quote was re-checked against the fetched page text; Andorra, Austria, Uruguay, Venezuela, Guatemala and Jamaica are not cross-checked; Paraguay is 1992 in the other table; the United Kingdom date is England's; the Ecuador, Dominican Republic and El Salvador rows are approximate (narrow first regime, OCR text, no statute named).
